summary: Diff adds two new markdown files. First is a plan for a `brief-artifact` skill: chunk a large doc, code, or diff, have fresh readers write per-chunk JSON (summary, anchored claims, risks, least-confident), then render a layered brief; includes layout, scripts, workflow, evals. Second is a debug-loop playbook for Claude Code: verification-gated loops, context management (/clear after two failed corrections, /compact at ~60%), prompting tips, hooks, subagents, git bisect, anti-pattern table, staged recommendations, caveats.

claims.text: No existing skill in `skills/` re-presents artifacts as layered briefs; closest is `session-review`.
Reading path picks by size: under 4 chunks sequential, 4+ chunks one subagent per chunk.
Chroma Context Rot report (July 14, 2025) evaluated 18 frontier models and found performance degrades with input length.
Spracklen et al. USENIX Security 2025 found 19.7% of recommended packages across 576,000 samples were hallucinated.
Extended-thinking budgets: 'think' ~4,000, 'think hard' ~10,000, 'ultrathink' 31,999, per Simon Willison decompilation.
Plan caps chunk summary at 120 words, but this reader prompt schema says 80 words; schema documents may disagree.

risks.note: Compact at 60%, auto-compact at ~80% attributed to unnamed practitioners; no source cited.
15x and ~4x subagent token multipliers and 80% variance figure cited without link; caveat admits context-specific.
2026 re-evaluation with 4.6-6.1% rates and 127 identical fake names has no named source.
Lost-in-the-middle 30+ point accuracy drop stated without citation.

least_confident: I could not check whether any of the quoted Anthropic doc passages, the Chroma report, or the USENIX study exist or say what the playbook attributes to them.
